clue.text: Quick look initially forgotten, probing historic rewritten document

indicators.note: something probing pushes inside, so these letters sit within the other word

parts.note: historic things belong to the past

indicators.note: what is forgotten at the start is the opening letter, so the word loses its head

parts.note: a glimpse is a brief look

explanation.surface: Someone takes a hurried peek at an old manuscript that has been rewritten.
explanation.walkthrough: Probing makes the shortened look sit inside the word for history, splitting it in two.
explanation.definitionFit: A palimpsest is a manuscript whose original writing was scraped off so the page could be written over again.

clue.text: Friend with a selection of food? It's very tasty

parts.note: a pal is a friend
taken as written
a table can mean the food laid out, as in keeping a good table

explanation.surface: A friend brings along a spread of dishes, and it is delicious.
explanation.definitionFit: Palatable describes food pleasant to eat, agreeable on the tongue and good enough to enjoy.

clue.text: Network behind schedule receiving reduced credit

indicators.note: a word receiving something takes it in, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: behind schedule means late

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: tick is informal British for credit, as in buying on tick

explanation.surface: A railway network running late while taking in less money than it hoped.
explanation.walkthrough: Buying on tick is British slang for buying on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: A lattice is a crisscross framework of strips, a mesh or grid pattern like a net.

clue.text: Mother joining three for bridge in rectory?

indicators.note: joining means placed next to, so the pieces are set side by side

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
bridge players sit at the compass points North, South, East and West; here three of them

explanation.surface: Mum makes up a four at the card table in the vicarage.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players are named after compass points, so three of them give N, S and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A manse is a minister's house, especially in Scotland, so a rectory is an example of the kind of home meant; hence the question mark.

clue.text: Pale young man in G&S upset — last performance?

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the other pair of letters
in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters read bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written: the initials of Gilbert and Sullivan
wan means pale
a son is a young male relative

explanation.surface: A pallid young lad is distressed in a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta, perhaps for his final show.
explanation.walkthrough: G&S is Gilbert and Sullivan, the Victorian writers of comic operas; only their initials are used.
explanation.definitionFit: A swansong is a final public appearance, from the myth that a swan sings just before death.

clue.text: Recap more than half of music?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, read cryptically: three of the five letters of music, written upwards in this down light

explanation.walkthrough: The second half works backwards from the answer: read as an instruction, it says the first word goes up, and SUM written upwards in a down entry gives MUS, more than half of music.
explanation.definitionFit: To sum up is to recap: to restate the main points briefly at the close of a talk.

clue.text: Sacred and hitherto largely seen in extreme instances

indicators.note: extreme instances are the outermost ones, so only each word's first and last letters are used

parts.note: first and last letters of hitherto
first and last letters of largely

explanation.surface: Something sacred has until now mostly appeared only in extreme cases.
explanation.walkthrough: Hitherto and largely look like adverbs modifying the sentence, but they are just the source words whose ends are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Holy means sacred: devoted to God or religion and treated with reverence.

clue.text: Handicraft engaging a million in the beginning? Not entirely

indicators.note: engaging can mean taking in or holding, so the other letters go inside
not entirely means incomplete, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: the origin is where something begins
taken as written
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: Was some craft involving a million folds there right from the start?
explanation.walkthrough: ORIGIN loses its last N to give ORIGI, which takes A and M inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the Japanese art of folding paper into shapes, a traditional craft done by hand.

clue.text: Produce that is left in yard

indicators.note: in places the first letters inside the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: YD is the abbreviation for yard
i.e. abbreviates Latin id est, that is
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A farmer points out the produce still lying in the yard.
explanation.definitionFit: Yield as a noun is the amount a crop or farm produces, its harvest or output.

clue.text: Thin meat? Reduced quantity served during flight

indicators.note: something served during an event happens inside it, so these letters go within the other word

parts.note: flight can mean running away, an escape

indicators.note: reduced means cut down, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a lot is a quantity or batch

explanation.surface: An airline serves smaller portions of meat on a flight.
explanation.walkthrough: Flight looks like air travel in the surface, but here it means fleeing.
explanation.definitionFit: An escalope is a thin boneless slice of meat, often veal, beaten flat and fried.

clue.text: English town turned out to be within borders of London

indicators.note: to be within means to sit inside, so these letters go between the others
the borders of a word are its edges, its first and last letters

parts.note: first and last letters of London

indicators.note: turned means rearranged, so the letters change their order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A place in England proved to lie just inside the outskirts of the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Luton is a town in Bedfordshire, north of London, known for its airport.
explanation.definitionFit: Luton is a large town in Bedfordshire, England, a place name rather than a city.

clue.text: Live broadcast of cities accepting King's truce

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the royal letter goes inside

parts.note: I am means I exist or live
R is short for rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Cities hear a live broadcast of the monarch announcing a ceasefire.
explanation.walkthrough: Live looks like an adjective for the broadcast, but it is a verb: 'I am' means I exist.
explanation.definitionFit: An armistice is a formal agreement to stop fighting, a truce or ceasefire between warring sides.

clue.text: Instant addition to communication shows muscle

parts.note: a trice is an instant, as in 'in a trice'
a PS, postscript, is added to the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A quick extra line on a message proves to be strong.
explanation.definitionFit: The triceps is the large muscle at the back of the upper arm that straightens the elbow.

clue.text: Notice vehicle impounded by LAPD at work

indicators.note: something impounded is locked up inside, so these letters sit within the others
at work means busy and in motion, so those letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A sign announces that the Los Angeles police have towed a car.
explanation.walkthrough: The LAPD is the Los Angeles Police Department, whose letters are scrambled here.
explanation.definitionFit: A placard is a poster or sign displayed in public, a written notice for people to read.

clue.text: Book, topping charts in audio format, full of compassion

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for book

indicators.note: in audio format means heard rather than read, so the spelling follows the sound

parts.note: a record topping the charts is leading them

explanation.surface: An audiobook that sits at number one is a deeply sympathetic story.
explanation.walkthrough: The sound of leading is respelt as LEEDING, as the bleed in bleeding sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A bleeding heart is someone whose sympathy for others is overflowing, so bleeding conveys deep pity.

clue.text: Dead routine for a woman? That's the American preference

definitions.note: the answer is a plural noun meaning one's preference

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for dead
a rut is a dull fixed routine
something for a woman is hers

explanation.surface: A woman complains that a dull daily grind is apparently what Americans like.
explanation.definitionFit: Druthers is an informal US word for one's choice, from 'I'd rather', as in 'if I had my druthers'.

clue.text: Poignant moment: victory in fighting at last

parts.note: mo is short for moment, as in 'half a mo'
V is the abbreviation for victory
taken as written

indicators.note: at last points to the very end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: last letter of fighting

explanation.surface: A touching scene as a fighter finally wins after a long struggle.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving means stirring the emotions, touching the heart in the way something poignant does.

clue.text: Consumer pursuing opening to get contribution to housewarming?

indicators.note: pursuing means coming after, so this piece follows the other

parts.note: a gash is a cut or opening
an eater consumes food

explanation.surface: A guest following the door to a new home brings a present for the housewarming party.
explanation.walkthrough: Housewarming is read literally: an appliance that warms a house, not a party gift.
explanation.definitionFit: A heater that burns gas literally warms a house, which is what the question mark flags.

clue.text: Staff's methodology to secure area for promotional tour

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast inside, so the letter goes within

parts.note: a rod is a staff, plus the S of the possessive
A is the abbreviation for area
the how of a thing is its method

explanation.surface: Employees plan how to book a region for a marketing tour.
explanation.walkthrough: Staff looks like employees, but it is a stick: ROD'S, holding A, then HOW.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadshow is a touring event that promotes a product, cause or programme from place to place.

clue.text: Each and every Parisian gets to visit a restaurant

parts.note: EA is the abbreviation for each
tout is French for every or all

explanation.surface: Every person in Paris gets to go to a restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat out is to have a meal away from home, typically at a café or restaurant.

clue.text: Dressmaker's encouragement to be audacious?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: what a dressmaker says when urging a customer to put on a garment
second meaning: British slang for cheekily testing how much one can get away with

explanation.walkthrough: In British English, to try it on is to chance one's arm, attempting something cheeky to see if it is tolerated.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both an invitation to put clothes on to check the fit and an idiom for impudently pushing one's luck.

clue.text: Delightful examples: nothing is false here

parts.note: love is a score of nothing in tennis
something false lies, tells untruths

explanation.surface: Charming specimens, and there is nothing untrue about them.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovelies is an informal plural noun for attractive people or things, beautiful specimens.

clue.text: Republican, beset by aggrieved purist, breaks in

indicators.note: beset means surrounded, so the single letter sits inside the other letters
aggrieved means upset and disturbed, so these letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A Republican politician, hounded by an indignant stickler, barges into a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: To irrupt is to burst or force one's way into a place suddenly, entering violently.

clue.text: Nonsense about variable work — here's a source of play

indicators.note: about means going around, so the first word surrounds the next letter

parts.note: tosh is British slang for nonsense
y is a standard algebraic variable
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Rubbish about flexible hours: this is where the fun comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: Tosh is British slang for nonsense; it wraps round Y, then OP follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop selling playthings supplies children with what they need for games, so it is a place where play comes from.

clue.text: Amount to pay to get around river goblin

indicators.note: to get around means to go round the outside, so these letters enclose the next one

parts.note: a toll is a charge to pay, as on a road or bridge
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: The fee to cross the river is demanded by the goblin under the bridge, as in the fairy tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A troll is an ugly creature from Scandinavian folklore, a kind of goblin or giant living under bridges.

clue.text: Explosive with no d_____ strength

indicators.note: with no means lacking, so the named letter is taken away

parts.note: gunpowder, or powder for short, is an explosive
the blanked word shows only its first letter, D

explanation.surface: An explosive without its expletive, still packing a punch.
explanation.walkthrough: The d_____ looks like a censored swear word, but it simply supplies the letter D to remove from POWDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Power means strength or force, the capacity to exert physical might.

clue.text: Very nasty creature brought in to finish legal separation

indicators.note: brought in means put inside, so these letters go within the next word

parts.note: to die is to finish or come to an end
V is the abbreviation for very
an orc is a monster from fantasy fiction

explanation.surface: A really horrible person was hired to end a marriage in the courts.
explanation.definitionFit: A divorce is the legal dissolution of a marriage, formally ending the couple's union.

clue.text: Very bad act gathering good indication of disapproval?

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for very

indicators.note: gathering means collecting in, so the letter goes inside the word

parts.note: a sin is a wrongful act
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A really terrible performance draws a gesture of contempt.
explanation.walkthrough: The V-sign, two fingers raised with the palm inward, is a rude British gesture of contempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Made with the back of the hand outward, the British two-fingered gesture is an insulting show of scorn.

clue.text: Extra bit of plant mutated in Trough Two

indicators.note: mutated means changed in form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener notices a strange extra shoot on a plant growing in the second trough.
explanation.definitionFit: An outgrowth is something growing out from a plant or body, an offshoot or protrusion.

clue.text: Feed information to one crackpot seizing power

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing hold of, so the letter is enclosed by the word

parts.note: a nut is a crazy person
P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: Someone briefs a lunatic who has grabbed control.
explanation.definitionFit: To input is to enter data into a computer or system, supplying it with facts.

clue.text: Some wood, including Northern pine

indicators.note: including means taking in, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: a log is a piece of wood
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: A forest including northern pine trees.
explanation.walkthrough: Pine looks like a kind of tree in a woodland picture, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to yearn or ache for it, which is the verb sense of pine.

clue.text: Sycophant interrupting toasts with no hesitation

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so these letters go inside the following word

parts.note: browns as a verb means toasts, as with bread
taken as written
er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A flatterer cuts in on the speeches at a dinner without pausing.
explanation.walkthrough: With no hesitation reads as a phrase meaning promptly, but NO and ER are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A brown-noser is slang for a toady who curries favour by obsequious flattery.
